approved_text: Is it true that for all sufficiently large n, one can choose a residue a_p for each prime p ≤ n such that every integer m with 1 ≤ m ≤ n satisfies m ≡ a_p (mod p) for at least two primes p ≤ n?
draft: Is it true that for all sufficiently large n, one can choose a residue a_p for each prime p ≤ n such that every integer m with 1 ≤ m ≤ n satisfies m ≡ a_p (mod p) for at least two primes p ≤ n?
source_docstrings:
Let `n` be sufficiently large. Is there some choice of congruence class `a_p` for all primes
`2 ≤ p ≤ n` such that every integer in `[1,n]` satisfies at least two of the congruences
`≡ a_p (mod p)`?
source_lean:
theorem erdos_689 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in .atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n,
      2 ≤ (Finset.Icc 1 n |>.filter fun p => p.Prime ∧ a p ≡ m [MOD p]).card
